newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end higher on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end higher on U.S. data.

text.p: French shares closed almost one percent up on Thursday, on the back of U.S. employment data which confirmed the bullish mood in the Paris market, traders said.

The CAC index took its lead from firm bond markets after U.S. jobs and wages statistics pointed to weak inflationary pressures. The CAC ran up with strong gains on Wall Street, building on the morning gains.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 27.53 points or 0.95 percent at 2,936.98. The CAC-40 futures contract closed up 22 at 2,939 from Wednesday's close.

Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux lost 1.45 percent to 611 francs, following Wednesday's announcement in Britain of a special "windfall tax" on privatised utilities. The group said the levy would not affect the group's profit forecast of net attributable profit above 3.5 billion francs for 1997.
Generale des Eaux was unchanged at 757 francs. The company said its British water firms fell outside the levy.
Eridania-Beghin was busy with a block trade 322,000 shares changing hands at 903 francs. The stock closed up 2.03 percent at 904.
Usinor adds 0.87 percent to 104.90, reversing earlier profit-taking.
LVMH rose 3.67 percent to 1,638, following Wednesday's meeting between the heads of LVMH, Guinness and Grand Met which raised hopes of the French group being brought into the British mega-merger.
Thomson-CSF rose 4.09 percent to 163 on hopes the government may yet privatise the defence electronics firm.
